name: AL-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 15 points, a steep structural hurdle for the challenger
Incumbent Dale Strong holds a 2-to-1 fundraising edge and a better than 5-to-1 cash advantage
Prediction markets give Andrew Sneed only about a 5 percent chance
No public polls or expert ratings track the race; Sneed's $860K haul signals interest but little cash on hand
model.rationale: An R+15 Alabama seat with a well-funded incumbent, no polling suggesting competition, and markets pricing Sneed near five percent leaves little room for an upset; the challenger's fundraising is respectable but has not translated into a visible race.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending for Sneed or new polling showing a single-digit contest would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's fifth district is a deeply Republican seat, and incumbent Dale Strong enters the general election with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean favors Republicans by roughly fifteen points, Strong has out-raised Democrat Andrew Sneed and holds a better than five-to-one cash advantage, and prediction markets give Sneed only a small chance of an upset. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals.

Sneed has raised a respectable sum for a challenger in this territory, which signals some Democratic interest, but little of it remains on hand and no outside groups have entered on his behalf. Barring an unexpected shift in the national environment or a late infusion of outside money, Strong is positioned for a comfortable win.
